items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: Milton had gotten me this job... Milton Romer to the front... he got me the job at the Glen Island Casino... Ozzie Nelson had the job, and his manager, a fellow by the name of Milton Romer, took a liking to me and he said, 'You get a band together and we'll put you in here...'

ctx.x: I see. And how about -- I'm looking for which book I found it in. I think it was George Simon's book. Said the reason you left there was that they wanted you to play softer and you wouldn't, and so they set up some guys in the red light district, some guys in your band, and busted them, and then the band had to leave town. Is that right?

No. There was a setup of a kind, but the way it happened was Seymour Weiss called Milton Romer and said, 'Look, will you get this band out of here? They're driving me crazy.' So Milton went along, he called and said, 'Look, I've got a job for you in Miami Beach. Would you like
to work there?" And I said, "Oh, yeah." He said, "Well, give your notice." He was in cahoots with Weiss, see? There wasn't any job in Miami Beach. We gave our notice, and of course we were out.
